core.title: Cover every acceptance commit-failure cause in the user/system flow
core.given: A user/system flow plan artifact whose flow reaches the acceptance commit at the Acceptance Authority boundary
core.when: the planner authors or revises the user/system flow's dispatch graph and acceptances
core.then: Each of the four acceptance commit-failure causes (version_conflict, authorization_refused, idempotency_conflict, authority_unavailable) is covered in the dispatch graph: reachable from the acceptance commit, registered, resolvable, and terminating.
prefer: Plan handling per cause: for each cause confirm its path (separate or shared) is registered, reachable, resolvable and terminating.
Treat commit-failure coverage as extending the user/system flow's coverage up to the Acceptance Authority boundary.
avoid: Covering only some of the four causes, or folding them into an unregistered generic failure path.
Paths that are registered but unreachable, reachable but unresolved, or that never terminate.
Deferrals without a tracking reference or expiry used to make coverage look complete.
unless: A specific cause has an explicit tracked-and-expiring deferral (excuses that cause only).
core.why: Acceptance commits can fail for four distinct reasons at the Acceptance Authority boundary; any cause that is unreachable, unregistered, unresolvable or non-terminating can strand the user/system flow.
evidence: For each of the four causes, the dispatch graph contains a registered path (dedicated or shared) reachable from the acceptance commit, with a resolution and a terminal state.
Any uncovered cause has its own deferral record with a tracking reference and an expiry that has not passed.
verification: Closed cause set: the acceptance commit-failure cause taxonomy is exactly {version_conflict, authorization_refused, idempotency_conflict, authority_unavailable}; a check must test all four causes individually, not as a group.
Four per-cause properties are checked: reachable, registered in the dispatch graph, resolvable, terminating. A shared handling path satisfies a cause if all four properties hold for that cause.
A deferral is accepted only if it is explicit, tracked and expiring, and it applies per cause (a deferral excuses only its own cause).
Automated per-cause validation is pending binding; until a validator exists, compliance with this rule is reviewer-judged, per cause.

values: user/system flow flow reaches the acceptance commit / Acceptance Authority boundary
commit-failure cause not reachable / not registered / not resolvable / not terminating, and not validly deferred

fires: A planner authors a user/system flow whose flow reaches an acceptance commit through the Acceptance Authority (whether or not the commit is the final step) and must plan handling for each commit-failure cause.
A user/system flow's dispatch graph handles version_conflict and authorization_refused but has no path or valid deferral for idempotency_conflict or authority_unavailable.
A planner revises a user/system flow and removes or reroutes a commit-failure handler so a cause no longer terminates.
doesNotFire: A user/system flow whose flow never reaches the acceptance commit / Acceptance Authority boundary.
Failure causes outside the acceptance commit-failure cause taxonomy (e.g. generic step failures), which are handled by other coverage conventions.

A user/system flow in which every one of the four causes is either covered (reachable, registered, resolvable, terminating) or has an explicit tracked-and-expiring deferral; a deferral excuses only its own cause.

neutralityNotes: This rule lives almost entirely at the method level: user/system flow, dispatch graph, acceptance commit, Acceptance Authority, and the closed cause taxonomy platform:acceptance:commit-failure.cause are ATDD-method concepts shared by every stack realization, so they stay in the core verbatim rather than becoming profile data (no vocabulary key fits and none is needed - they are semantics, not structure). The only stack-specific content is the repository-layout globs in activation.facts[1] (moved to roles.plan_artifact.path, with the .user-system-flow.yaml name pattern) and the D5 / #1089 validator-ownership references (bunOnly); the pending-binding, reviewer-judged enforcement status is kept generically in core:verification. The taxonomy identifier 'platform:acceptance:commit-failure.cause' was paraphrased as 'the acceptance commit-failure cause taxonomy' in then/verification to avoid implying a stack namespace, without changing the closed set.
